concepts.def: Recognised by FSMs; described by regular expressions.

walkthroughs.body_html: Noam Chomsky's hierarchy ranks grammars: type 3 regular, type 2 context-free, type 1 context-sensitive, type 0 recursively enumerable. Each level strictly contains the previous.
Most programming languages have a context-free core syntax expressed in BNF. CFGs can match nested parentheses — something regular grammars cannot do.
Regular languages are recognised by FSMs and described by regular expressions. They cannot count arbitrarily — they cannot check that every '(' has a matching ')'.
